finding.problem: name_release can be run again on a commit that already has a release name, and it overwrites that name. Nothing stops two commits from sharing one release name. The stated purpose is that people refer to a release by name instead of by commit id, so a reused or silently renamed name makes that reference ambiguous or wrong. This also sits badly with approval being permanent in the glossary, since the name tied to an approved commit can change at will.
finding.where: authoring/authoring.domain.yaml, actions.name_release (preconditions: approved-to-name, release-name-stated; effect set target.release_name)

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Seeded is none; overwriting a name and non-unique names are speculative design concerns the request never constrained (it only asks to let the owner give a name), not real defects.

finding.problem: The release name is stored on Commit but nothing else uses it. The deliver_approved_commit handoff and Delivery's DeliveryRequest still carry only the commit id, so a delivery cannot be referred to by release name. The glossary has no entry for 'release name'. No scenario or fixture exercises name_release: its approved-only denial, its empty-name denial and the successful case are all untested.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Not propagating the name to delivery, adding a glossary entry, or adding scenarios were not requested, so these are not real problems with this change.

edit.why: It adds release_name to Commit and a name_release action requiring approval, but the request is bound to record_approval (a name set when a commit is approved) and record_approval was not changed; also the edit appears to have dropped the 'main' field's type lines or garbled the field structure.
